div.div:
This specialized Task has two main responsibilities:
1. Go through and clear the hardware flags with NOTIFICATION criticality and report them as software flags using Error IDs through the Error Handler
2. Ensure all NOTIFICATION errors in the log are processed using the API offered by the Error Handler.
Task is called periodically in the Scheduler (within FDTI) by default and can optionally be called after completing the Startup routine to handle NOTIFICATION errors before starting Mission Mode.

div.div: The Notification Error Logger stores NOTIFICATION Error IDs for later retrieval, where the Process Notification Log API is used to go through all the NOTIFICATION errors in the log and issue the callback.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 218px; height: 1px; padding-top: 230px; margin-left: 942px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0px; text-align: left;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: normal;

div.div: The callbacks are application-specific and can be designed to handle all Error IDs either uniformly or with specialized responses for each, depending on the application's requirements. Possible actions include logging errors for later handling or transitioning the system into a Safe State after handling is completed.

div.div: Disables global interrupts, stores the Error ID causing the safe state transition for retrieval after reset, attempts a software reset and floating of the I/O pins in an infinite loop.
